content:
maria.g: heads up — started seeing a big spike in trivy failures around 07:12 UTC, lots of `image pull timeout` and then the scanner floods the registry. failed jobs piling up in the scanner-worker queue.
kevin.p: seeing same. errors in logs: ```
Jul 10 07:11:59 scanner-worker trivy: ERROR: failed to pull image "ghcr.io/repo/service:latest": Get \"https://ghcr.io/v2/repo/service/manifests/latest\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```
sre-bot: alert created: INC-3421 — scanner-worker image-pull-timeout storm (auto-detected 07:15 UTC) :rotating_light:
liz.z: quick question — are we hitting GHCR rate limits or is this our redis cache misbehaving? last week we saw cache keys getting evicted and then every scanner pod re-populated layers at once.
kevin.p: checked registry headers from failed attempts — some 429s interleaved with timeouts. but also trivy logs show: `cache miss` for the same blob across ~30 concurrent workers. smells like cache layer (redis) not sticky / keys TTL too short.
devsec: what does our suppression sync look like? if the sync lambda is retrying it could be blasting redis too.
maria.g: suppression-sync lambda started failing auth with KMS yesterday afternoon; errors were `AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt` when trying to read the suppression blob in S3. after that suppressions fallback -> full eval -> more network activity.
kevin.p: timeline fits. suppression-sync failing -> workers can't read suppression list -> more vulnerability checks -> registry / CVE DB hits spike -> image pulls/timeouts.
liz.z: quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce scanner concurrency back to 10 for now, 2) enable local disk cache on worker nodes (`--cache-dir /var/lib/trivy-cache`) so cold-start storms don't hit registry as hard, 3) re-deploy a temporary rate-limited job runner to warm cache. thoughts?
devsec: agree. also fix KMS perms ASAP. minimal IAM change: grant the suppression-sync role `kms:Decrypt` on the specific key (not *). We'll rotate the principal after. Need a PR to infra.
maria.g: patch plan: (A) scale down parallel scans from 50 -> 10 (k8s HPA tweak), (B) add `--cache-dir` mount to scanner DaemonSet + emptyDir with retention so pods reuse cache, (C) revert suppression-sync to older role binding we used last month while we debug KMS policy. I'll open a PR and a rollout plan.
kevin.p: test command for local repro: `trivy image --cache-dir /tmp/trivy-cache ghcr.io/repo/service:latest` — if that runs without repeated registry hits we’re good. Also add trivy flag `--skip-update` during warmup to avoid CVE DB hammering.
liz.z: for long-term: we should add per-repo rate limits and central cache (s3-backed blobstore) so workers get blobs from us instead of registry. + add circuit breaker so if registry 429s spike we backoff and queue.
devsec: on suppression & audit: once KMS perms fixed, run a full sync and validate via audit logs: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt` for the suppression-sync role. Also we should add an alert if suppression sync fails > 3 times in 30m.
maria.g: opened INC-3421 and PUT a short runbook in the incident thread. PR #2345 created for HPA + cache-dir change. rolling out to staging now.
kevin.p: rolling to staging confirmed, staging scanner pods started with `--cache-dir` and are hitting the mounted emptyDir. initial signs: fewer registry requests and lower median scan time. :thumbsup:
liz.z: we still have a high CVE flagged in one base image (CVE-2024-9999) — triage says high with exploitability = moderate. recommendation: bump base image and rebuild, but that’s a product change for the runtime team. can we temporarily add a scan-exception only after review?
devsec: exceptions allowed only after manual triage and a ticket with mitigations. If we add a suppression, store it in S3 encrypted by KMS and annotate with reviewer/expiry. No blanket suppressions.
maria.g: noted. I'll add the triage ticket and link it to the PR.
sre-bot: incident update INC-3421: mitigations applied (reduced concurrency, cache enabled). Monitor for 30m.
kevin.p: follow-up action items: 1) infra PR for KMS policy (least privilege) 2) add cache warm job 3) add circuit breaker logic to scanner 4) add suppression-sync alerting 5) schedule base-image bump for affected service. I'll create cards.
liz.z: thanks all — ping me if triage needs extra eyes.
maria.g: closing slack thread when monitoring window passes, will post final incident notes in postmortems channel.
